# Local pre-commit / pre-push hooks. Cheap mechanical checks run on
# every commit; heavyweight checks (pytest) on push only. The same
# hooks run in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` against every PR.
#
# Install once per checkout:
#   pip install pre-commit  # or `uv tool install pre-commit`
#   pre-commit install --install-hooks
#
# Skip a single hook with `SKIP=<id> git push`. Don't `--no-verify`
# — CI is the canonical gate and has none.

default_install_hook_types: [pre-commit, pre-push]
default_stages: [pre-commit]

repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/pre-commit/pre-commit-hooks
    rev: v6.0.0
    hooks:
      - id: trailing-whitespace
      - id: end-of-file-fixer
      - id: mixed-line-ending
        args: [--fix=lf]
      - id: check-yaml
      - id: check-json
      - id: check-merge-conflict
      - id: check-added-large-files
        args: [--maxkb=512]

  # Python lint + format. Configured via the [tool.ruff] block in
  # pyproject.toml at the repo root. Mirrors the CI Ruff / Ruff-format
  # steps.
  - repo: https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff-pre-commit
    rev: v0.15.12
    hooks:
      - id: ruff-check
        args: [--fix]
      - id: ruff-format

  # Bash lint. Repo convention is `*.bash`, not `*.sh`; override the
  # default file matcher.
  - repo: https://github.com/shellcheck-py/shellcheck-py
    rev: v0.11.0.1
    hooks:
      - id: shellcheck
        args: [-x, -S, warning]
        types: [file]
        files: \.bash$

  # Bash format. `-d` runs in diff mode so the hook fails if the file
  # isn't formatted, without rewriting it.
  - repo: https://github.com/scop/pre-commit-shfmt
    rev: v3.13.1-1
    hooks:
      - id: shfmt
        args: [-i=4, -ci, -d]
        types: [file]
        files: \.bash$

  # pytest as a pre-push hook (too slow for every commit). Mirrors the
  # CI Pytest step.
  - repo: local
    hooks:
      - id: pytest
        name: pytest (plugins/autocuda/tests)
        entry: bash -c 'PYTHONPATH=plugins/autocuda/lib python3 -m pytest plugins/autocuda/tests/ -q'
        language: system
        pass_filenames: false
        stages: [pre-push]
name: CI

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  pre-commit:
    name: pre-commit hooks
    runs-on: self-hosted
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.11"
      - name: Install pre-commit
        run: python -m pip install pre-commit
      - name: Run pre-commit on changed files
        # On PRs, lint the diff against `main`. On `push` to main, lint
        # the whole repo. The diff scope on PRs keeps the gate fast and
        # avoids historic-file noise; the full-repo scan on main keeps
        # drift from sneaking in.
        run: |
          if [ "${{ github.event_name }}" = "pull_request" ]; then
            git fetch origin "${{ github.base_ref }}" --depth=1
            pre-commit run --from-ref "origin/${{ github.base_ref }}" --to-ref HEAD
          else
            pre-commit run --all-files
          fi

  pytest:
    name: pytest
    runs-on: self-hosted
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.11"
      - name: Install Graphviz and Pandoc
        # `viz graph` needs the system Graphviz binaries (dot/neato/sfdp/twopi/
        # circo) plus pygraphviz's build headers. `report html` requires Pandoc.
        # CI installs both so it exercises the real renderers rather than
        # skipping their integration tests.
        run: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y graphviz graphviz-dev pandoc
      - name: Install test dependencies
        run: python -m pip install pytest matplotlib pandas adjustText pygraphviz
      - name: Run plugin tests
        run: PYTHONPATH=plugins/autocuda/lib python3 -m pytest plugins/autocuda/tests/ -q

  package:
    name: pip package
    runs-on: self-hosted
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.11"
      # pygraphviz (an autocuda dependency) builds against the system
      # Graphviz headers, so installing the package needs them present.
      - name: Install Graphviz
        run: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y graphviz graphviz-dev
      - name: Build and install the package
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip
          python -m pip install .
      - name: Smoke-test the console script and the plugin installer
        # `autocuda --help` proves the entry point + lib/ path shim resolve and
        # that it lists the `install` verb; `autocuda install` with no host CLI
        # present must warn per-host and exit 0.
        run: |
          autocuda --help | grep -q install
          autocuda install
[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"

[project]
name = "autocuda"
version = "0.4.0"
description = "Autonomous CUDA optimization agent plugin: skills, a CLI, and the Claude Code, Codex, and Pi installer."
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.10"
license = "Apache-2.0"
authors = [{ name = "Bryce Adelstein Lelbach" }]
keywords = ["cuda", "gpu", "optimization", "benchmarking", "agent-skills"]
dependencies = [
    # The CLI's renderers. `viz progress` needs matplotlib + pandas +
    # adjustText; `viz graph` additionally needs pygraphviz (which binds to
    # the system Graphviz libraries — see README "Install"). They are bundled
    # here so a `pip install` of this package is enough to run every CLI verb.
    "matplotlib",
    "pandas",
    "adjustText",
    "pygraphviz",
]

[project.scripts]
autocuda = "autocuda_pkg._entry:main"

[project.urls]
Homepage = "https://github.com/brycelelbach-private/autocuda"
Repository = "https://github.com/brycelelbach-private/autocuda"

# The CLI modules under plugins/autocuda/lib are flat, bare-name siblings
# (`from _log import ...`); the entry point puts that dir on sys.path at
# call time rather than installing them as top-level modules (which would
# collide with other packages). force-include bundles the whole plugin
# payload — lib/, agents/ (the Codex subagent TOML the installer copies),
# skills/, and the marketplace manifest — inside the autocuda_pkg package.
[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["autocuda_pkg"]

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel.force-include]
"plugins/autocuda" = "autocuda_pkg/plugins/autocuda"

# Ruff configuration for the autocuda CLI (including the bundled
# dashboard and plot subcommands) and ci helpers. pre-commit's
# `ruff-check` and `ruff-format` hooks pick this up automatically
# (ruff walks up from each file to find the nearest pyproject.toml).

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 100
target-version = "py310"

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
    "E",   # pycodestyle
    "F",   # pyflakes
    "W",   # warnings
    "I",   # isort
    "B",   # bugbear
    "UP",  # pyupgrade
]
ignore = [
    "E501",  # line too long — handled by the formatter
]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
# Tests are allowed to use bare asserts, magic numbers, and longer
# fixtures without ruff complaining.
"plugins/autocuda/tests/*" = ["B011"]
# AutoCUDA

AutoCUDA is an agentic system for optimizing real-world CUDA applications with no prior knowledge of them. It uses a multi-agent parallel tree search process to explore the breadth of possible implementations in search of speed of light performance.

To install the AutoCUDA CLI and its Claude Code, Codex, and Pi integrations from NVIDIA's internal GitLab:

```bash
pip install "git+https://gitlab-master.nvidia.com/blelbach/autocuda.git"
autocuda install
```

Or from GitHub (requires access to the repo):

```bash
pip install "git+https://github.com/brycelelbach-private/autocuda"
autocuda install
```

`autocuda install` registers the marketplace plugin with Claude Code and Codex, installs the Codex worker definition, and registers the bundled Pi package and Pi worker definition when each host is available.

Then from your harness run:

```text
/autocuda:optimize-tree repo=nvidia/cccl benchmark=histogram workers=4
```

## Skills

autocuda ships a set of agentskills.io-compatible workflows:

- **`autocuda:discover`** — map an unfamiliar CUDA project; produce the ground-truth layout the optimization loop consumes.
- **`autocuda:optimize-simple`** — run the autonomous trial loop: modify source, validate, benchmark, keep-or-revert, log, repeat. The inner loop most operators wrap with `optimize-hill`.
- **`autocuda:optimize-hill`** — manager skill that runs `optimize-simple` as a worker sub-agent and keeps it from stopping. The recommended entry point for unattended single-process runs.
- **`autocuda:optimize-tree`** — parallel tree-search: a manager writes one structured brief at a time (objective + parent commit + macro/micro classification), each with a global brief id, and spawns one `optimize-tree-worker` sub-agent per brief — each running the `autocuda:explore-brief` skill — to execute it; workers record trials in per-brief logs, the manager judges the results and either pushes the same worker on its brief or writes a fresh diverse brief for a new worker, keeping N briefs in flight. The brief-diversity check is what prevents the search from collapsing into N hill-climbers around the same local max. GPU-bound commands serialise via `autocuda run`.
- **`autocuda:explore-brief`** — the worker skill each `optimize-tree-worker` sub-agent runs: branch off the brief's parent commit, then iterate edit → build → validate → benchmark → profile → commit → log under the brief's objective, and return its measurements to the manager. The worker executes and measures; the manager judges whether the idea has merit and what to try next.
- **`autocuda:simplify`** — minimize the diff between a baseline (upstream) and an optimized branch without regressing performance. A thin wrapper over `optimize-tree`: the same manager loop and workers, but the run carries a second `optimized` reference alongside the baseline and the fleet drives a `diff_lines` benchmark down with `simplify` briefs (and `macro` / `micro` / `combine` when a simplification opens a new optimization).
- **`autocuda:combine`** — cherry-pick the best optimizations across multiple optimize branches onto one composite branch.
- **`autocuda:crawl`** — search the public Internet for CUDA candidate repos and bootstrap an autocuda-`<name>` fork for each one that passes discover.
- **`autocuda:report-{optimization,behavior,cost,reward-hacking,skill}`** — produce CSV / markdown / HTML reports across one or more experiment branches.
- **`autocuda:viz`** — render an optimize-tree run's strategic "run map" with `autocuda viz graph`, writing the short plain-language descriptions of the run's top optimizations that the graph's legend shows (the CLI badges them; the skill is what makes them readable to someone with no background on the run).
- **`autocuda:export`** — create or update `autocuda/export/<tag>` snapshots of the `autocuda/` data directory (binary artefacts excluded). An existing branch receives one true delta commit when captured data changes and no commit when it does not; every branch selected in one invocation is populated from the same immutable source capture. When `repo=<slug-or-url>[@<branch>]` is supplied, export validates ancestry and pushes with an exact lease so it cannot overwrite a concurrent remote update. Without `repo=`, export starts from local `main` and stays local. Each snapshot also bundles a self-contained static `dashboard.html` and — unless `memory=false` (`--no-memory`) — agent-harness session memory under `harness-records/memory/{claude,codex}/`, best-effort secret-scrubbed first (`scrub=false` / `--no-scrub` to skip).

## CLI

AutoCUDA also provides a CLI that the skills drive and operators use directly:

- **`autocuda init`** — materialise the `autocuda/` data directory for single-skill runs, write `worker-limits.json`, and launch the dashboard on the first free port from 8000 upward (skippable with `--no-dashboard`). Run once at the start of a session.
- **`autocuda init {manager,brief}`** — `manager --workers <N>` materialises the optimize-tree data directory and `worker-limits.json` (the uniform per-build cap and the fan-out width N) without pre-creating any worktrees; `brief --tag <tag> --brief-id <K>` cherry-picks brief `<K>`'s parent commit onto a fresh `autocuda/optimize/<tag>/brief-<K>` branch in a per-brief worktree it creates on demand (regardless of CWD) and emits `WORKTREE` / `BRANCH` / `BRIEF` / `BRIEF_KIND` / `BRIEF_ID` / `PARENT_COMMITS` / `MODE` / `PARENT_METRIC_<bench>` / `PARENT_PROFILE` lines workers `eval` directly. `MODE` is `fresh` for a new branch or `resume` when an open brief is being re-entered after a crash.
- **`autocuda schema {define,check}`** — write the per-project log and report schemas at startup; validate logs, report data CSVs, report markdown, `layout.md`, `environment.md`, and exports against them.
- **`autocuda log <skill> ...`** — append rows to a skill's `*-log.csv`; the first write for a tag captures `<tag>-optimize-schema.json`, and every later write for that run enforces the same immutable benchmark schema. For optimize-tree the verb takes a sub-verb: `autocuda log optimize-tree {baseline,optimized,brief,trial,start,stop}` (`optimized` records a simplify run's second reference).
- **`autocuda run {slice,exclusive}`** — run a command under per-GPU locks so concurrent workers coordinate on a node's GPUs. `slice` builds inside the fleet's uniform CPU/memory cap (from `worker-limits.json`) and yields to any benchmark on any GPU; `exclusive` claims any *free* GPU for a benchmark, pins `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` to it, and blocks builds everywhere and other benchmarks on the *same* GPU while benchmarks on *different* GPUs run concurrently. The GPU count lives in `gpu-count`; benchmarks load-balance across GPUs rather than pinning each worker to one.
- **`autocuda status --tag <tag>`** — print JSON fleet state from the manager, reference, and per-brief logs. `global_best` starts at the baseline (or simplify reference) and changes when a complete successful trial sets a higher measured record; `best_trial` and `top_best` list branchable trial commits even when all are slower than the reference. The model-facing `progress` object has exactly three fields: `balance` is search-tree balance from 0 (one collapsed tip) to 1 (evenly spread), or null only when the tree cannot be built; `recent_improvement_percent_per_trial` is the compounded exact-record growth rate over the trailing `max(2 * workers, 10)` complete successful trials (using all such trials so far for a younger run, and null before the first); and `stalled` is true whenever that recent improvement rate is less than 1.0% per trial. The rate uses direction-normalized aggregate speedup, so the same definition covers maximize, minimize, multi-benchmark, and simplify runs. Failed trials and succeeded rows missing a commit or any active benchmark are ignored. Requiring every active benchmark prevents, for example, a result that measured only one of a run's two benchmarks from being ranked against complete results. Optimize-tree log writers resolve commit/ref arguments through Git and persist the full 40-character lowercase SHA for every commit and parent identity. The manager runs status once after a worker completion, then either continues that brief or, when stalled, uses the freed slot for a different parent and idea. `--top <K>` limits `top_best`, `--top 0` returns every ranked trial, and `--as-of <iso>` pins "now" for replay/tests. Stdout remains JSON-only; the throttled skill reminder remains on stderr.
- **`autocuda candidates ...`** — manage the persistent crawl candidate database (`autocuda/crawl-database.csv`).
- **`autocuda report data {optimization,behavior,cost,skill}`** / **`autocuda report html`** — build the report data CSVs the `report-*` skills consume, and convert written report markdown to an atomic, standalone styled HTML document. Optimization reports accept lowercase 7- to 40-character Git SHAs in experiment logs, resolve abbreviated identities through Git, and write canonical full identities to report data. CSS is embedded; Mermaid diagrams use a version-pinned CDN runtime and therefore need network access when viewed.
- **`autocuda export [--tag <tag>]`** — create or incrementally update a selected snapshot, or omit `--tag` to discover every run. Each invocation captures the source once, writes a true delta to every changed branch, and leaves unchanged branches at the same commit. Temporary source captures and sibling worktrees are removed after success and after errors. `--memory` (default on; `--no-memory` to skip) bundles the harness's Claude Code / Codex session memory under `harness-records/memory/{claude,codex}/`, best-effort secret-scrubbed (`--scrub` / `--no-scrub`); the live-secret scan runs regardless and refuses to commit on a match.
- **`autocuda export daemon {start,stop}`** — `start` periodically runs one no-tag export sweep so all discovered tag and report routes share one captured source state; `--interval` defaults to `4h`, `--foreground` keeps the loop attached, and `--max-ticks` bounds attached runs. `stop` validates the recorded process identity and stops the daemon plus an active export child. `.export-daemon.pid`, `.export-daemon.lock`, and the rotating `export-daemon.log` remain local sidecars and are excluded from snapshots.
- **`autocuda dashboard {start,stop}`** — daemonized HTTP dashboard for every `*-log.csv` under `--data-dir`. The live index loads the current run immediately, loads historical runs and raw log tables when opened, and conditionally refreshes only visible run data that changed. A header menu discovers every rendered `<output>-report-*.html`, groups the reports by output, derives labels from their filenames, and opens them in new tabs; newly added report kinds need no dashboard changes. The same relative links work in an exported static `dashboard.html`. optimize-tree logs render as a tidy-tree search view of briefs and their trials (cards on a `(depth, row)` grid with cubic-bezier connectors, the path to the global best highlighted as an amber "spine"; a combine brief draws one dashed edge per parent it stacks, and when the combine sits on the spine those fan-in edges are amber too) over a score-over-time strip. Log writers resolve refs and persist full 40-character lowercase Git SHAs; the dashboard accepts valid 7- to 40-character identities, while malformed or unresolved identities degrade safely. Concurrent handlers, bounded idle waits, and per-render error markers keep a bad run or idle client from blocking the service. The reference log remains internal scoring context, while each manager and brief log is available below the tree. `autocuda init` launches this automatically, so the typical operator flow doesn't need an explicit `dashboard start`.
- **`autocuda viz {progress,graph}`** — render an experiment run as a PNG. `viz progress <csv>` is the tactical best-so-far chart for one run; it folds an optimize-tree manager log's per-brief siblings into one curve and requires a valid `log-schema-optimize.json` for benchmark direction. `viz graph` maps every accepted commit with a Graphviz engine. The full dependency ancestry of the global best is gold, including every combine input; ambiguous commit prefixes fail, and excluding a reward-hacking commit taints its descendants and combine dependants. Milestones in that ancestry are badged and described from a validated `--labels` JSON. `--engine all` atomically publishes the complete PNG set, while a failed engine publishes none. Resolve the manager log with `--tag`/`--data-dir` or pass it positionally; `--list-milestones` emits JSON without rendering. Needs the system Graphviz binaries (`dot`/`neato`/`sfdp`/`twopi`/`circo`).

Typical flow: `discover` → `optimize-hill` (or `optimize-simple` directly) → optionally `combine` to cross-pollinate multiple optimize branches → optionally `simplify` to minimize the patch against upstream without losing performance → `report-*` to look at the results → `export` to snapshot everything onto a portable branch. `crawl` is an independent entry point that drives discover automatically across many candidate repos.

### Artifacts

Every file the skills write lands under `autocuda/` at the repo root. `<tag>` is the run tag a skill chose at startup — a UTC timestamp in `%Y-%m-%d-%H-%M-%S` format (e.g. `2026-04-05-14-32-01`). The `autocuda log` and `autocuda export` CLIs enforce this format; passing a `--tag` that doesn't match (e.g. one accidentally suffixed with the skill name) is rejected.

```
autocuda/
├── layout.md                               written by discover; the machine-agnostic
│                                           ground-truth project description every
│                                           downstream skill reads (a project may commit
# autocuda plugin

The autocuda plugin for Agent Skills-compatible hosts. Ships the `autocuda:discover`, `autocuda:optimize-simple`, `autocuda:optimize-hill`, and `autocuda:optimize-tree` skills, plus `autocuda:explore-brief`, `autocuda:simplify`, `autocuda:combine`, `autocuda:crawl`, the five `autocuda:report-*` skills, and `autocuda:export`, alongside the `optimize-tree-worker` sub-agent the `optimize-tree` manager spawns (which runs `autocuda:explore-brief`). `discover` maps an unfamiliar CUDA project and produces `autocuda/layout.md` (machine-agnostic project description) plus `autocuda/environment.md` (machine-specific GPU / timings / profiler half); `optimize-simple` runs the autonomous optimization trial loop against those; `optimize-hill` manages `optimize-simple` for unattended long runs; `optimize-tree` runs a parallel tree-search by keeping N briefs in flight, each executed by its own `optimize-tree-worker` sub-agent, with manager-written briefs classified as macro, micro, combine, or simplify and kept diverse; `simplify` is an `optimize-tree` run carrying a second `optimized` reference whose fleet drives the diff against the baseline (upstream) down without regressing performance; `report-skill` audits run transcripts for bugs in autocuda skill instructions and skill-to-CLI contracts; `export` snapshots the `autocuda/` data directory onto a portable branch, using `repo=<slug-or-url>[@<branch>]` as the optional source and push target, and (unless `memory=false`) also bundles the agent harness's Claude Code / Codex session memory under `harness-records/memory/{claude,codex}/`, best-effort secret-scrubbed, when an ephemeral workspace is about to be torn down.

Every export updates selected snapshot branches by default: changed snapshots receive one true delta commit and unchanged snapshots are no-ops, with all branches in one invocation populated from one immutable source capture. `autocuda export daemon start` periodically runs one no-tag sweep and `autocuda export daemon stop` validates and stops its recorded process group. The PID, lock, and rotating log sidecars remain local and are excluded from exported data.

The worker sub-agent ships in three host formats: `agents/optimize-tree-worker.md` for Claude Code, `agents/optimize-tree-worker.toml` for Codex, and `agents/pi/optimize-tree-worker.md` for Pi's `pi-subagents` package. **Codex plugins do not install subagent TOMLs**, so `autocuda install` copies the TOML into `~/.codex/agents/`. The same command registers `package.json` with Pi so Pi loads the skills and `pi-subagents` discovers its worker. Every format is a thin wrapper that runs the `autocuda:explore-brief` skill.

The plugin also ships an `autocuda` CLI that the skills drive and operators use directly. `autocuda status` exposes one model-facing `progress` object with exactly `balance` (0 for one collapsed tip through 1 for an even spread, or null when unavailable), `recent_improvement_percent_per_trial` (compounded exact-record growth per complete successful trial over the trailing stall window, or null before the first), and `stalled` (true whenever that recent rate is less than 1.0% per trial); failures and incomplete measurements are ignored. See the main repo README for the per-subcommand list; the other operator-facing entry points are `autocuda dashboard start` / `autocuda dashboard stop` (a daemonized HTTP dashboard that loads the current run immediately, loads historical runs and raw tables when opened, conditionally refreshes visible data, auto-discovers every rendered `<output>-report-*.html` in a new-tab header menu that also works in static exports, resolves commit/ref inputs to full 40-character lowercase Git SHAs, treats malformed or unresolved identities as missing lineage, isolates render failures and idle clients across bounded concurrent requests, and renders optimize-tree briefs and their trials as a tidy-tree search view — spine = path to the global best, briefs labelled with their kind (macro / micro / combine / simplify) — over a score-over-time strip whose running-best line starts at the baseline, with a per-brief log dropdown beneath the merged tree plus one for the reference log; the reference-log baseline is shown once and brief_start / brief_stop are kept out of the graph; each benchmark's speedup direction is read from `log-schema-optimize.json`) and `autocuda viz {progress,graph}` (`viz progress <csv>` is a 'best so far' PNG progress chart for an individual run, which also reads unit/direction from `log-schema-optimize.json`; `viz graph` is the strategic whole-run map of an optimize-tree search — every accepted commit a node laid out by a Graphviz engine, the path to the global best a gold line, merges diamonds, node fill the commit's brief kind, and the run's top optimizations badged and described in a side legend from the `autocuda:viz` skill's `--labels` JSON — resolving commits from the log's own `commit` column so it also works on an exported snapshot; needs the system Graphviz binaries).

The CLI ships as a pip package: `pip install "git+https://github.com/brycelelbach-private/autocuda"` puts `autocuda` on PATH and pulls its Python dependencies (matplotlib, pandas, adjustText, pygraphviz, plus the system Graphviz libraries). Then `autocuda install` registers this plugin with whichever of Claude Code, Codex, and Pi is present and installs each host's worker definition. It is the explicit host-registration step after the Python package install.

For installation, usage, and the example CUDA benchmarks the skills were developed against, see the main repo README:
<https://github.com/brycelelbach-private/autocuda>

#!/home/ubuntu/.local/share/uv/tools/autocuda/bin/python3
"""`autocuda install` — register the agent plugin with every host.

A `pip install` puts the CLI and its Python dependencies in place, but the
*skills* are discovered by the agent host, not by Python. Claude Code and
Codex read a plugin marketplace, while Pi reads a local package. This command performs those host
registrations so one `pip install` + `autocuda install` leaves a host able
to invoke the `autocuda:*` skills:

  * Claude Code — `claude plugin marketplace add <repo>` +
    `claude plugin install <plugin>@<marketplace> --scope user`.
  * Codex — `codex plugin marketplace add <repo>` +
    `codex plugin add <plugin>@<marketplace>`, then copy the worker
    subagent TOML into `~/.codex/agents/` (Codex plugins do not install
    subagent definitions themselves).
  * Pi — expose the bundled plugin at a stable user path, then register it
    with `pi install` so Pi loads the skills and pi-subagents discovers the
    worker definition.

Every step degrades to a warning rather than an error when a host binary
is absent or a registration returns non-zero, so installing on a
Claude-only or Codex-only box — or re-running — is safe and idempotent.
The command returns 0 even when a host is missing, so the autonomous
agent bootstrap can run it unconditionally after installing the harnesses.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from autocuda_pkg import plugin_root

# The marketplace repo (hosts .claude-plugin/marketplace.json at its root),
# the marketplace name that manifest declares, and the plugin within it.
MARKETPLACE_REPO = "brycelelbach-private/autocuda"
MARKETPLACE_NAME = "brycelelbach-autocuda"
PLUGIN_NAME = "autocuda"
# Worker subagent the optimize-tree manager launches; Codex reads custom
# subagents from ~/.codex/agents/<name>.toml.
SUBAGENT_TOML = "optimize-tree-worker.toml"
PI_PACKAGE_LINK = Path(".local/share/autocuda/pi-package")


def _warn(msg: str) -> None:
    print(f"warning: {msg}", file=sys.stderr)


def _run(cmd: list[str]) -> bool:
    """Run a host command, streaming output. True on exit 0, else warn."""
    try:
        proc = subprocess.run(cmd, check=False)  # noqa: PLW1510 (check handled)
    except OSError as exc:
        _warn(f"{cmd[0]} failed to launch: {exc}")
        return False
    if proc.returncode != 0:
        _warn(f"`{' '.join(cmd)}` returned {proc.returncode}")
        return False
    return True


def _install_for_host(host_bin: str, repo: str) -> None:
    """`<host> plugin marketplace add` + install/add, mirroring how the
    bootstrap installs plugins. `claude` uses `plugin install ... --scope
    user`; `codex` uses `plugin add`."""
    if not _run([host_bin, "plugin", "marketplace", "add", repo]):
        _warn(
            f"{host_bin} marketplace add {repo} did not succeed "
            "(no access to a private repo, or already added) — continuing."
        )
    if host_bin == "claude":
        _run(
            [host_bin, "plugin", "install", f"{PLUGIN_NAME}@{MARKETPLACE_NAME}", "--scope", "user"]
        )
    else:
        _run([host_bin, "plugin", "add", f"{PLUGIN_NAME}@{MARKETPLACE_NAME}"])


def _install_codex_subagent() -> None:
    """Copy the worker subagent TOML into ~/.codex/agents/. Codex plugins
    don't install subagent definitions, so the manager can't launch the
    `optimize-tree-worker` type until this file is in place."""
    src = plugin_root() / "agents" / SUBAGENT_TOML
    if not src.is_file():
        _warn(f"bundled subagent {src} missing; skipping Codex subagent install.")
        return
    dest_dir = Path(os.path.expanduser("~/.codex/agents"))
    try:
        dest_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        shutil.copyfile(src, dest_dir / SUBAGENT_TOML)
    except OSError as exc:
        _warn(f"could not install Codex subagent into {dest_dir}: {exc}")
        return
    print(f"Installed Codex subagent: {dest_dir / SUBAGENT_TOML}")


def _install_pi_package(pi_bin: str) -> None:
    """Expose the bundled payload at a stable path and register it with Pi."""
    src = plugin_root()
    manifest = src / "package.json"
    if not manifest.is_file():
        _warn(f"bundled Pi package manifest {manifest} missing; skipping Pi plugin install.")
        return

    dest = Path.home() / PI_PACKAGE_LINK
    try:
        dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        temporary_link = dest.with_name(f".{dest.name}.{os.getpid()}.tmp")
        if temporary_link.exists() or temporary_link.is_symlink():
            temporary_link.unlink()
        temporary_link.symlink_to(src, target_is_directory=True)
        os.replace(temporary_link, dest)
    except OSError as exc:
        _warn(f"could not expose the Pi package at {dest}: {exc}")
        return

    if _run([pi_bin, "install", str(dest)]):
        print(f"Installed Pi package: {dest}")


def install_plugins(
    repo: str = MARKETPLACE_REPO,
    *,
    claude: bool = True,
    codex: bool = True,
    pi: bool = True,
) -> int:
    """Register the plugin with every selected host that is present.
    Returns 0 always — a host being absent is not an error, since the
    autonomous agent bootstrap runs `autocuda install` unconditionally after
    installing the harnesses and it must never fail when one is missing."""
    did_something = False
    if claude and shutil.which("claude"):
        print("Registering the autocuda plugin with Claude Code…")
        _install_for_host("claude", repo)
        did_something = True
    elif claude:
        _warn("claude not on PATH; skipping Claude Code plugin registration.")
    if codex and shutil.which("codex"):
        print("Registering the autocuda plugin with Codex…")
        _install_for_host("codex", repo)
        _install_codex_subagent()
        did_something = True
    elif codex:
        _warn("codex not on PATH; skipping Codex plugin registration.")
    pi_bin = shutil.which("pi") if pi else None
    if pi_bin:
        print("Registering the autocuda package with Pi…")
        _install_pi_package(pi_bin)
        did_something = True
    elif pi:
        _warn("pi not on PATH; skipping Pi package registration.")
    if not did_something:
        _warn(
            "none of `claude`, `codex`, or `pi` was found on PATH; the autocuda CLI is "
            "installed, but no host plugin was registered. Re-run `autocuda "
            "install` once a host CLI is available."
        )
    return 0


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog="autocuda install",
        description="Register the autocuda agent plugin with Claude Code, Codex, and Pi.",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--repo",
        default=MARKETPLACE_REPO,
        help=f"marketplace repo (owner/name). Default: {MARKETPLACE_REPO}.",
    )
    only = parser.add_mutually_exclusive_group()
    only.add_argument("--claude-only", action="store_true", help="register only with Claude Code.")
    only.add_argument("--codex-only", action="store_true", help="register only with Codex.")
    only.add_argument("--pi-only", action="store_true", help="register only with Pi.")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    only_selected = args.claude_only or args.codex_only or args.pi_only
    return install_plugins(
        args.repo,
        claude=args.claude_only or not only_selected,
        codex=args.codex_only or not only_selected,
        pi=args.pi_only or not only_selected,
    )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# Local pre-commit / pre-push hooks. Cheap mechanical checks run on
# every commit; heavyweight checks (pytest) on push only. The same
# hooks run in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` against every PR.
#
# Install once per checkout:
#   pip install pre-commit  # or `uv tool install pre-commit`
#   pre-commit install --install-hooks
#
# Skip a single hook with `SKIP=<id> git push`. Don't `--no-verify`
# — CI is the canonical gate and has none.

default_install_hook_types: [pre-commit, pre-push]
default_stages: [pre-commit]

repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/pre-commit/pre-commit-hooks
    rev: v6.0.0
    hooks:
      - id: trailing-whitespace
      - id: end-of-file-fixer
      - id: mixed-line-ending
        args: [--fix=lf]
      - id: check-yaml
      - id: check-json
      - id: check-merge-conflict
      - id: check-added-large-files
        args: [--maxkb=512]

  # Python lint + format. Configured via the [tool.ruff] block in

  # steps.
  - repo: https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff-pre-commit
    rev: v0.15.12
    hooks:
      - id: ruff-check
        args: [--fix]
      - id: ruff-format

  # Bash lint. Repo convention is `*.bash`, not `*.sh`; override the
  # default file matcher.
  - repo: https://github.com/shellcheck-py/shellcheck-py
    rev: v0.11.0.1
    hooks:
      - id: shellcheck
        args: [-x, -S, warning]
        types: [file]
        files: \.bash$

  # isn't formatted, without rewriting it.
  - repo: https://github.com/scop/pre-commit-shfmt
    rev: v3.13.1-1
    hooks:

        types: [file]
        files: \.bash$

  # CI Pytest step.
  - repo: local

# AutoCUDA

AutoCUDA is an agentic system for optimizing real-world CUDA applications with no prior knowledge of them. It uses a multi-agent parallel tree search process to explore the breadth of possible implementations in search of speed of light performance.

To install the AutoCUDA CLI and its Claude Code, Codex, and Pi integrations from NVIDIA's internal GitLab:

```bash
pip install "git+https://gitlab-master.nvidia.com/blelbach/autocuda.git"
autocuda install
```

Or from GitHub (requires access to the repo):

```bash
pip install "git+https://github.com/brycelelbach-private/autocuda"
autocuda install
```

`autocuda install` registers the marketplace plugin with Claude Code and Codex, installs the Codex worker definition, and registers the bundled Pi package and Pi worker definition when each host is available.

Then from your harness run:

```text
/autocuda:optimize-tree repo=nvidia/cccl benchmark=histogram workers=4
```

## Skills

autocuda ships a set of agentskills.io-compatible workflows:

- **`autocuda:discover`** — map an unfamiliar CUDA project; produce the ground-truth layout the optimization loop consumes.
- **`autocuda:optimize-simple`** — run the autonomous trial loop: modify source, validate, benchmark, keep-or-revert, log, repeat. The inner loop most operators wrap with `optimize-hill`.
- **`autocuda:optimize-hill`** — manager skill that runs `optimize-simple` as a worker sub-agent and keeps it from stopping. The recommended entry point for unattended single-process runs.
- **`autocuda:optimize-tree`** — parallel tree-search: a manager writes one structured brief at a time (objective + parent commit + macro/micro classification), each with a global brief id, and spawns one `optimize-tree-worker` sub-agent per brief — each running the `autocuda:explore-brief` skill — to execute it; workers record trials in per-brief logs, the manager judges the results and either pushes the same worker on its brief or writes a fresh diverse brief for a new worker, keeping N briefs in flight. The brief-diversity check is what prevents the search from collapsing into N hill-climbers around the same local max. GPU-bound commands serialise via `autocuda run`.
- **`autocuda:explore-brief`** — the worker skill each `optimize-tree-worker` sub-agent runs: branch off the brief's parent commit, then iterate edit → build → validate → benchmark → profile → commit → log under the brief's objective, and return its measurements to the manager. The worker executes and measures; the manager judges whether the idea has merit and what to try next.
- **`autocuda:simplify`** — minimize the diff between a baseline (upstream) and an optimized branch without regressing performance. A thin wrapper over `optimize-tree`: the same manager loop and workers, but the run carries a second `optimized` reference alongside the baseline and the fleet drives a `diff_lines` benchmark down with `simplify` briefs (and `macro` / `micro` / `combine` when a simplification opens a new optimization).
- **`autocuda:combine`** — cherry-pick the best optimizations across multiple optimize branches onto one composite branch.
- **`autocuda:crawl`** — search the public Internet for CUDA candidate repos and bootstrap an autocuda-`<name>` fork for each one that passes discover.
- **`autocuda:report-{optimization,behavior,cost,reward-hacking,skill}`** — produce CSV / markdown / HTML reports across one or more experiment branches.
- **`autocuda:viz`** — render an optimize-tree run's strategic "run map" with `autocuda viz graph`, writing the short plain-language descriptions of the run's top optimizations that the graph's legend shows (the CLI badges them; the skill is what makes them readable to someone with no background on the run).
- **`autocuda:export`** — create or update `autocuda/export/<tag>` snapshots of the `autocuda/` data directory (binary artefacts excluded). An existing branch receives one true delta commit when captured data changes and no commit when it does not; every branch selected in one invocation is populated from the same immutable source capture. When `repo=<slug-or-url>[@<branch>]` is supplied, export validates ancestry and pushes with an exact lease so it cannot overwrite a concurrent remote update. Without `repo=`, export starts from local `main` and stays local. Each snapshot also bundles a self-contained static `dashboard.html` and — unless `memory=false` (`--no-memory`) — agent-harness session memory under `harness-records/memory/{claude,codex}/`, best-effort secret-scrubbed first (`scrub=false` / `--no-scrub` to skip).

## CLI

AutoCUDA also provides a CLI that the skills drive and operators use directly:

- **`autocuda init`** — materialise the `autocuda/` data directory for single-skill runs, write `worker-limits.json`, and launch the dashboard on the first free port from 8000 upward (skippable with `--no-dashboard`). Run once at the start of a session.
- **`autocuda init {manager,brief}`** — `manager --workers <N>` materialises the optimize-tree data directory and `worker-limits.json` (the uniform per-build cap and the fan-out width N) without pre-creating any worktrees; `brief --tag <tag> --brief-id <K>` cherry-picks brief `<K>`'s parent commit onto a fresh `autocuda/optimize/<tag>/brief-<K>` branch in a per-brief worktree it creates on demand (regardless of CWD) and emits `WORKTREE` / `BRANCH` / `BRIEF` / `BRIEF_KIND` / `BRIEF_ID` / `PARENT_COMMITS` / `MODE` / `PARENT_METRIC_<bench>` / `PARENT_PROFILE` lines workers `eval` directly. `MODE` is `fresh` for a new branch or `resume` when an open brief is being re-entered after a crash.
- **`autocuda schema {define,check}`** — write the per-project log and report schemas at startup; validate logs, report data CSVs, report markdown, `layout.md`, `environment.md`, and exports against them.
- **`autocuda log <skill> ...`** — append rows to a skill's `*-log.csv`; the first write for a tag captures `<tag>-optimize-schema.json`, and every later write for that run enforces the same immutable benchmark schema. For optimize-tree the verb takes a sub-verb: `autocuda log optimize-tree {baseline,optimized,brief,trial,start,stop}` (`optimized` records a simplify run's second reference).
- **`autocuda run {slice,exclusive}`** — run a command under per-GPU locks so concurrent workers coordinate on a node's GPUs. `slice` builds inside the fleet's uniform CPU/memory cap (from `worker-limits.json`) and yields to any benchmark on any GPU; `exclusive` claims any *free* GPU for a benchmark, pins `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` to it, and blocks builds everywhere and other benchmarks on the *same* GPU while benchmarks on *different* GPUs run concurrently. The GPU count lives in `gpu-count`; benchmarks load-balance across GPUs rather than pinning each worker to one.
- **`autocuda status --tag <tag>`** — print JSON fleet state from the manager, reference, and per-brief logs. `global_best` starts at the baseline (or simplify reference) and changes when a complete successful trial sets a higher measured record; `best_trial` and `top_best` list branchable trial commits even when all are slower than the reference. The model-facing `progress` object has exactly three fields: `balance` is search-tree balance from 0 (one collapsed tip) to 1 (evenly spread), or null only when the tree cannot be built; `recent_improvement_percent_per_trial` is the compounded exact-record growth rate over the trailing `max(2 * workers, 10)` complete successful trials (using all such trials so far for a younger run, and null before the first); and `stalled` is true whenever that recent improvement rate is less than 1.0% per trial. The rate uses direction-normalized aggregate speedup, so the same definition covers maximize, minimize, multi-benchmark, and simplify runs. Failed trials and succeeded rows missing a commit or any active benchmark are ignored. Requiring every active benchmark prevents, for example, a result that measured only one of a run's two benchmarks from being ranked against complete results. Optimize-tree log writers resolve commit/ref arguments through Git and persist the full 40-character lowercase SHA for every commit and parent identity. The manager runs status once after a worker completion, then either continues that brief or, when stalled, uses the freed slot for a different parent and idea. `--top <K>` limits `top_best`, `--top 0` returns every ranked trial, and `--as-of <iso>` pins "now" for replay/tests. Stdout remains JSON-only; the throttled skill reminder remains on stderr.
- **`autocuda candidates ...`** — manage the persistent crawl candidate database (`autocuda/crawl-database.csv`).
- **`autocuda report data {optimization,behavior,cost,skill}`** / **`autocuda report html`** — build the report data CSVs the `report-*` skills consume, and convert written report markdown to an atomic, standalone styled HTML document. Optimization reports accept lowercase 7- to 40-character Git SHAs in experiment logs, resolve abbreviated identities through Git, and write canonical full identities to report data. CSS is embedded; Mermaid diagrams use a version-pinned CDN runtime and therefore need network access when viewed.
- **`autocuda export [--tag <tag>]`** — create or incrementally update a selected snapshot, or omit `--tag` to discover every run. Each invocation captures the source once, writes a true delta to every changed branch, and leaves unchanged branches at the same commit. Temporary source captures and sibling worktrees are removed after success and after errors. `--memory` (default on; `--no-memory` to skip) bundles the harness's Claude Code / Codex session memory under `harness-records/memory/{claude,codex}/`, best-effort secret-scrubbed (`--scrub` / `--no-scrub`); the live-secret scan runs regardless and refuses to commit on a match.
- **`autocuda export daemon {start,stop}`** — `start` periodically runs one no-tag export sweep so all discovered tag and report routes share one captured source state; `--interval` defaults to `4h`, `--foreground` keeps the loop attached, and `--max-ticks` bounds attached runs. `stop` validates the recorded process identity and stops the daemon plus an active export child. `.export-daemon.pid`, `.export-daemon.lock`, and the rotating `export-daemon.log` remain local sidecars and are excluded from snapshots.
- **`autocuda dashboard {start,stop}`** — daemonized HTTP dashboard for every `*-log.csv` under `--data-dir`. The live index loads the current run immediately, loads historical runs and raw log tables when opened, and conditionally refreshes only visible run data that changed. A header menu discovers every rendered `<output>-report-*.html`, groups the reports by output, derives labels from their filenames, and opens them in new tabs; newly added report kinds need no dashboard changes. Concurrent handlers, bounded idle waits, and per-render error markers keep a bad run or idle client from blocking the service. The reference log remains internal scoring context, while each manager and brief log is available below the tree. `autocuda init` launches this automatically, so the typical operator flow doesn't need an explicit `dashboard start`.
- **`autocuda viz {progress,graph}`** — render an experiment run as a PNG. `viz progress <csv>` is the tactical best-so-far chart for one run; it folds an optimize-tree manager log's per-brief siblings into one curve and requires a valid `log-schema-optimize.json` for benchmark direction. `viz graph` maps every accepted commit with a Graphviz engine. The full dependency ancestry of the global best is gold, including every combine input; ambiguous commit prefixes fail, and excluding a reward-hacking commit taints its descendants and combine dependants. Milestones in that ancestry are badged and described from a validated `--labels` JSON. `--engine all` atomically publishes the complete PNG set, while a failed engine publishes none. # autocuda contributor guide for AI coding agents

This file is read by Claude Code (via `CLAUDE.md` symlink resolution) and other AGENTS.md-aware harnesses (Codex, Aider, etc.). The conventions below apply to every change, regardless of which agent wrote it.

## Scope is the operator's call, not yours

Agents do not get to decide what work belongs in a PR. The operator's instruction is the scope; the answer is "ship a complete fix".

- **Never push back on an instruction because it's "too big".** When the operator describes a multi-file change, a sweep across skills, or a refactor with broad blast radius, the answer is "ok, doing it" — not "this is a lot, want to split into multiple PRs?", not "this expands #N's scope considerably, are you sure?", not a numbered list of clarifying questions. Plan the work, do the work, surface unknowns inside the work (in commit messages or the PR body), not in a pre-flight Q&A. Operator scope decisions are final on first instruction.
- **Never ask "if you say do it, I'll go" or its variants.** If you've reached the point of describing what you'd do in detail and inviting the operator to greenlight it, you have already wasted a turn — start with the work instead. The operator's original instruction is the greenlight. Phrases like "want me to land this in #N or as a follow-up?", "let me know if anything looks off", "if anything looks off, say so" are forbidden when used as a confirmation gate before action; they are fine *after* the work is done as a sanity check.
- **Do all the work the instruction implies.** If the operator says "rename skill X to Y", that includes every README / plugin.json / marketplace.json reference, not just the skill directory rename. If the operator says "add CLI flag F to subcommand S", that includes the `Namespaces` block, the `--help` text, the test, and every skill that should now use the flag instead of inventing the value itself. A change shipped without its consequences is incomplete, not "scoped".

Specifically banned, in PR bodies, commit messages, issue comments, design docs, and code comments:

- *Out of scope* / *out-of-scope* (any capitalization), as a section header or inline qualifier.
- *Follow-up PR* / *follow-up issue*, used to defer work that the current change should have included.
- *Left for later* / *leaving X for a separate PR* / *deferred to a future change*.
- *Future work* sections in design docs that list things the current PR should have done.
- *Deliberately not addressing X here* / *not in scope* — the operator decides scope, not the agent.

If a change is *truly* independent — an orthogonal cleanup the agent noticed in passing, with its own diff and its own test path — it belongs in its own PR opened in parallel, not in a "scope note" appended to the current one. The bar for "independent" is high: if dropping the orthogonal change makes the current PR's test plan honest about what's tested vs. broken, it isn't independent.

## No backwards compatibility

autocuda is pre-1.0 and has no external users running off its schemas, CSV layouts, branch names, or CLI surface. We do not preserve old shapes across renames. When the design changes, the codebase changes — there is no migration window, no deprecation period, and no compatibility shim layer.

Concretely, in any PR that renames or restructures a thing:

- **No legacy aliases.** When a column / flag / status / argument / file path is renamed, the old name disappears. Don't add `row.get("agent_id") or row.get("worker_id")` fallbacks, don't keep a `--deprecated-alias` next to the new flag, don't accept both old and new header names in CSV readers.
- **No version branching for the migration period.** If a schema or on-disk format changes, the new version is what the codebase reads and writes. Don't keep a "version 1 fallback path" alive on the assumption old runs need to keep working — they don't.
- **No "graceful warning" for the old shape.** A caller passing the old shape gets an error, not a warning that papers over the rename. The agent reading the error then fixes the call site.
- **No deprecation comments.** Removed code stays removed. `# Deprecated, will be removed in vX` and `# kept for backward compat` are forbidden — those just defer the cleanup that should have landed in the same diff.
- **No re-exports of moved symbols.** When a function moves modules, callers update.
- **Tests update too.** A test fixture that constructs the old shape is part of the rename, not exempt from it. The whole test suite reflects current code.

The only exception is genuinely external interfaces we don't own: the GitHub API, kernel `flock` semantics, `nsys` / `ncu` output formats, the on-disk format of git objects. Those we accept as we find them. Everything inside `autocuda/` — log schemas, CSV column headers, branch namespaces, CLI flags, skill argument names, profile filename conventions — is fair game to change without an upgrade path.

If a rename is genuinely too large to land in one PR, that means the PR scope is wrong (split it into independently-renamable units), not that the codebase needs a transitional layer.

## Style

### Issues

- Close issues from the PR via `Closes #N.` in the PR body — don't manually close before merge. Multiple issues each need their own keyword: `Closes #1, #2.` only closes #1 and treats the bare `#2` as a mention, so write `Closes #1. Closes #2.` (or `Closes #1, closes #2.`) to pick up both.

### Documentation

When a change touches user-visible surface, update the docs that describe it in the **same PR** — don't leave the docs as a follow-up:

- **A new or renamed skill** → update the top-level `README.md` (the `## How it works` skill list, the `### Artifacts` and `### Branches` trees if applicable, and the `## Project structure` block listing the skill directory), `plugins/autocuda/README.md`, `plugins/autocuda/.claude-plugin/plugin.json`'s description, `plugins/autocuda/.codex-plugin/plugin.json`'s description, `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`'s description, and `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` if the marketplace metadata changes.
- **A new or renamed sub-agent** (a definition under `plugins/autocuda/agents/`, e.g. `optimize-tree-worker` that the `optimize-tree` manager spawns) → update the same `README.md` surfaces (the `## How it works` entry for the manager skill that spawns it and the `## Project structure` `agents/` listing), `plugins/autocuda/README.md`, and every manager skill that spawns it by `name` or by `agents/<name>.md` path. The agent's `name:` frontmatter is the `subagent_type` the manager launches — rename it and the manager's launch call must follow.
- **A new or renamed CLI subcommand or flag** → update the module docstring at the top of `plugins/autocuda/lib/autocuda_cli.py` (the `Namespaces` block) and the `help=` text on every affected argparse parser. The `--help` output is the agent's primary discovery surface — keep it accurate.
- **A change to the on-disk layout** (new file kind under `autocuda/`, new branch namespace, new schema) → update the README's `### Artifacts` and / or `### Branches` trees so the layout is auditable at a glance.
- **A change to the contributor flow** (new pre-commit / pre-push hook, a new required setup step, a new style rule) → update this file (`AGENTS.md`) so the next agent picks the rule up automatically.

The rule is: if `git diff main` shows a user-visible change, `git diff main -- README.md plugins/autocuda/README.md AGENTS.md` should show a doc update on the same line of work. If it doesn't, the PR is incomplete.

### Avoid documenting history

**Documenting history in source is strictly forbidden.** Code and design documents describe what *is*, not what *was*. Git contains the history; PR descriptions explain the change; issue threads carry the discussion. Don't duplicate that into the tree.

If a sentence's meaning depends on the reader knowing what this file or the surrounding code used to say, it's history — delete it. The test is mechanical: cover the rest of the document, read the sentence on its own, ask *"does this still make sense to someone who has never seen the prior version?"* If no, the sentence is history.

- No `# previously this …` / `# changed from … to …` / `# this used to be a …` comments. Same ban on the prose equivalents — *"a previous version of this"*, *"this used to"*, *"until recently"*, *"we removed"*, *"the old behaviour was"*.
- No "we tried X but switched to Y because Z" prose. State Y. The reason it isn't X belongs in the PR that made the switch.
- No motivation-by-history — don't justify the present rule by what it replaced (*"this is strict because the old version got abused"*). The rule is its own justification; design pressure that shaped it goes in the PR description, not the doc.
- No `(see #NN)` / `(#NN fixed this)` parentheticals embedded in docstrings, help text, or skill prose — those are PR-description material. Cross-references *to currently-open* issues for known-bug behaviour are fine; cross-references to *closed* issues that motivated a rule are not.
- No bug-incident write-ups embedded in source. The post-mortem belongs in the PR that fixed the bug.
- No incident counts or audit statistics. *"Polling shells were the worst offender in the harness audit that filed this rule — 25 occurrences across 6 worker JSONLs in one run"* is history dressed up as evidence; the rule stands or falls on its own statement. State the rule, period.
- No "this rule was filed because …" / "the audit that produced this rule found …" / "we found N instances of …" framing. These are PR-description sentences that wandered into the source.
- Removed code stays removed. Don't comment it out, don't `# (removed in #NN)` it.

A reader walking into the file cold should see only what's true now. If they need the history, `git log` and `git blame` are one keystroke away. If a rule needs evidence to justify it, that evidence belongs in the PR description, the linked issue, or both — never in the source tree.

### Skill prose: be concise, defer detail

The top-level SKILL.md for each skill is loaded into the agent's context every time the skill runs. Token cost compounds across the iterative skills (`optimize-simple`, `optimize-tree`, `simplify`, `combine`, `explore-brief`) because they re-read the skill on every iteration (see the *Re-read* rule in each loop). `explore-brief` in particular is loaded into every worker the `optimize-tree` manager spawns. Budget tokens accordingly.

- **Lead with what the agent must do**, in the imperative. State the rule, then stop. No motivation paragraphs, no "this is here because", no "in the past we tried X".
- **Cap subsections.** Each `###` subsection under `## Optimization strategy` / `## Constraints` / `## Operating rules` is at most ~5 short paragraphs. If it grows past that, the load-bearing rule is buried — extract.
- **Detail goes in `references/<topic>.md`**, not in SKILL.md. The skill prose names the topic, points at the reference, and moves on. Examples of progressive disclosure already in the tree: `references/profilers.md` (full `nsys` / `ncu` invocation form), `references/libraries.md` (the CUDA library catalogue). When a new long-form explanation would otherwise land in a SKILL.md, write a new reference file instead and cite it.
- **No examples in skill prose unless the example is load-bearing.** A reader who already knows what an `nsys` invocation looks like doesn't need to see one in SKILL.md; they need to know *which* invocation form to use, and the reference file has that.
- **Cite, don't restate.** If a rule already lives in another skill or in `references/`, point at it. Two copies of the same rule drift apart and the reader gets both at double the token cost.
- **Use `name=value` for skill arguments.** In `argument-hint` and skill invocation prose, write skill arguments as `repo=<path>` / `agent-id=<N>`. Reserve `--flag` syntax for actual shell commands and CLI examples.

The check: open the diff for any SKILL.md change. If a paragraph could be replaced by *"see `references/<topic>.md`"* and the skill would still tell the agent what to do, replace it.

### Placeholder spelling in skill prose

Three placeholder styles appear in skill prose; mixing them within the same skill creates noise. The convention is:

- **Type/shape placeholders** — `<N>`, `<path>`, `<slug>`, `<value>`, `<name>` — describe the *shape* of a value the caller supplies. Use these in `argument-hint` and on first definition of an argument: `workers=<N>`, `data-dir=<path>`, `repo=<slug>|<path>`.
- **Argument-name placeholders** — `<tag>`, `<agent-id>`, `<data-dir>` — refer back to an argument by its noun. Use these in body prose once the argument has been introduced: *"every worker uses the same `<tag>`"*, *"the worker cds into `<data-dir>`"*.
- **Shell variables** — `$TAG`, `$DATA_DIR` — appear only inside fenced shell snippets, and only after a visible `NAME=...` capture step in the same skill (e.g. `eval "$(autocuda init manager --workers 3)"`).

Always backtick `<placeholder>` tokens in prose so they're never mistaken for HTML. Don't introduce a fresh placeholder name (`<id>`) when the argument's actual name (`agent-id`) is already in scope — refer back by the argument's name, not a paraphrase.

### Markdown style

- **No artificial line wrapping** in prose. One paragraph = one long line. Some older files in the tree still hard-wrap at ~80 chars; touching them is an opportunity to unwrap, but don't make a separate PR for it. New prose ships unwrapped.
- **ATX headings** (`# H1`, `## H2`, `### H3`) — never setext (`===` / `---` underlines).
- **Dash bullets** (`- foo`), not asterisks or plus.
- **Fenced code blocks** with a language tag where it's meaningful (` ```bash`, ` ```python`, ` ```text`). Plain ``` is fine for shell snippets without a clear language.
- **No trailing whitespace, no tabs.** The pre-commit `trailing-whitespace` and `mixed-line-ending` hooks enforce this.

### Pre-commit and pre-push hooks

The repo gates `git commit` and `git push` with mechanical checks. Install once per checkout:

```bash
pip install pre-commit       # or `uv tool install pre-commit`
pre-commit install --install-hooks
```

`pre-commit install` wires the hooks into `.git/hooks/`. After that, `git commit` runs the pre-commit stage (whitespace, ruff, shellcheck) and `git push` runs the pre-push stage (pytest). The same set of hooks runs in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` against every PR.

Skip a single hook with `SKIP=<id> git commit` (e.g. `SKIP=ruff-format git commit`). Don't `--no-verify` — CI is the canonical gate and has none.

**Resolving marketplace issues**

I'm dealing with a marketplace manifest name collision. An option could be to create an ephemeral copy of the marketplace JSON with a renamed marketplace name. But it seems I shouldn't hand-edit the marketplace config. I might look into the plugin-creator helper for updates, but I don’t want to make PR changes. Removing the existing remote marketplace and adding a local checkout sounds simpler. I can keep the same name after removing it, ensuring a clean configuration. I'll also consider using a cache buster after the commit.

**Navigating deployment challenges**

The user asked about a PR and deploying locally, but having a dirty deployment-only manifest isn't ideal. I wonder if I can create a symlink or a copy for a local source plugin. When adding plugins, it seems they get copied into a cache. If I update the manifest, I'll need to revert the source afterward. The user suggested applying a patch for edits, but I'm not sure if modifications are allowed. I could possibly work with a temporary copy in /tmp to avoid dirtying the source. That could keep things cleaner overall.

**Managing plugin marketplace stability**

I'm considering the scenario where the local and temporary plugin marketplace paths may get deleted, which could break the configured marketplace. I could keep the temporary version stable under `/.local/share/autocuda-dev-marketplace`, but that might be overengineering. It seems Codex might support adding a marketplace plugin using `owner/repo --ref branch`, and just removing and re-adding could suffice without needing a cachebuster if the revision is different. However, the generic plugin creator mentions that a cachebuster is essential for updating existing local plugins. That feels a bit confusing!

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# autonomous-agent-bootstrap global git hook dispatcher. Configured by
# bootstrap.bash and pointed to by the global core.hooksPath. Every git hook
# name is a symlink to this one script.
#
# On pre-commit it (1) blocks commits whose author / committer identity (and,
# when global signing is on, whose signing config) does not match the global
# git config the bootstrap set up, and (2) blocks commits that stage a secret,
# scanning the staged diff with gitleaks (or a built-in shell-grep fallback).
# For every hook it then chains to the repository's own .git/hooks/<name> so
# project hooks keep running, since a global core.hooksPath replaces rather than
# supplements the per-repo hooks directory.
set -uo pipefail

hook_name=$(basename -- "$0")

# Extract a field from a `git var GIT_*_IDENT` value, formatted as
# "Name <email> <unixtime> <tz>".
_aab_ident_field() {
    case "$2" in
        name)  printf '%s' "$1" | sed -E 's/ <[^>]*> [0-9]+ [-+][0-9]+$//' ;;
        email) printf '%s' "$1" | sed -E 's/.*<([^>]*)> [0-9]+ [-+][0-9]+$/\1/' ;;
    esac
}

# Block the commit unless the author and committer identity match the global
# git config, and unless the globally-configured signing is honored. The
# expected values come from --global, which `git -c`, GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS,
# and a repo-local config cannot override; the actual values come from
# `git var`, which reflects `--author` and GIT_AUTHOR_*/GIT_COMMITTER_* env
# vars that the effective `git config user.email` does not.
_aab_enforce_commit_identity() {
    local exp_name exp_email
    exp_name=$(git config --global --get user.name 2>/dev/null || true)
    exp_email=$(git config --global --get user.email 2>/dev/null || true)

    # Nothing pinned in the global config — nothing to enforce.
    if [ -z "$exp_name" ] && [ -z "$exp_email" ]; then
        return 0
    fi

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Rewrite a local plugin version to a single Codex cachebuster suffix."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import re
import sys
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path


CACHEBUSTER_PREFIX = "codex"


def parse_args() -> argparse.Namespace:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description=(
            "Rewrite a local plugin's version so it preserves everything before '+' and uses "
            "a single +codex.<cachebuster> suffix."
        )
    )
    parser.add_argument("plugin_path", help="Path to the plugin root directory")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--cachebuster",
        help="Optional cachebuster token to embed in the plugin version",
    )
    return parser.parse_args()


def main() -> None:
    args = parse_args()
    plugin_root = Path(args.plugin_path).expanduser().resolve()
    manifest_path = plugin_root / ".codex-plugin" / "plugin.json"
    manifest = load_manifest(manifest_path)

    version = manifest.get("version")
    if not isinstance(version, str) or not version.strip():
        raise ValueError(f"{manifest_path} must contain a non-empty string 'version'.")
    cachebuster = sanitize_cachebuster(args.cachebuster or default_cachebuster())
    next_version = with_cachebuster(version, cachebuster)
    manifest["version"] = next_version
    manifest_path.write_text(json.dumps(manifest, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")

    print(f"Updated plugin version: {version} -> {next_version}")


def load_manifest(manifest_path: Path) -> dict[str, object]:
    if not manifest_path.is_file():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"missing manifest: {manifest_path}")
    payload = json.loads(manifest_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    if not isinstance(payload, dict):
        raise ValueError(f"{manifest_path} must contain a JSON object.")
    return payload
def sanitize_cachebuster(value: str) -> str:
    sanitized = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9-]+", "-", value.strip().lower())
    sanitized = re.sub(r"-{2,}", "-", sanitized).strip("-")
    if not sanitized:
        raise ValueError("Cachebuster must contain at least one letter or digit.")
    return sanitized


def default_cachebuster() -> str:
    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y%m%d%H%M%S")


def with_cachebuster(version: str, cachebuster: str) -> str:
    version_prefix = version.split("+", 1)[0]
    return f"{version_prefix}+{CACHEBUSTER_PREFIX}.{cachebuster}"


if __name__ == "__main__":
    try:
        main()
    except Exception as err:  # noqa: BLE001 - CLI should surface a single clear message.
        print(str(err), file=sys.stderr)
        raise SystemExit(1) from err

        hook_types: list[str] | None,

        return

    try:
        _, out, _ = cmd_output(*diff_cmd, f'{old}...{new}')
